newsitem.title: USA: World 96/97 cotton use record 18.9 mln tonnes - ICAC.
newsitem.headline: World 96/97 cotton use record 18.9 mln tonnes - ICAC.

text.p: World cotton use will rise to a record 18.91 million tonnes (86.8 million bales) in 1996/97 from 18.522 million tonnes (85.1 million bales) in 1995/96, the International Cotton Advisory Committee (ICAC) said Monday.
Consumption is rising fastest in cotton-producing countries, including India, the United States, Turkey and Mexico, ICAC said in its monthly report.
"An encouraging sign for future increases in cotton use is that consumption is rising this season in Central Europe and Russia," the report added.
World cotton production was estimated at 18.85 million tonnes (86.6 million bales) in 1996/97, down from 19.912 million tonnes (91.5 million bales) in 1995/96, because of a reduction in harvest area.
Changes in production and reduced imports by China, had begun to shift the pattern of world trade in cotton, the report said.
Uzbekistan's and the United States' share of world exports were falling, with French-speaking Africa, Australia and India likely to see an increase, it said.
